A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Task Vector Bases work. All 36 pages of v4 and 42 pages of v5, including their appendices, support comparison. Text, equations, tables, and retained figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v4 reports original vision and language merging, OOD generalization, continual learning, and negation experiments, with additional analyses and generative-language-model results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds profiling, precision, QLoRA compatibility, encoder-ablation, and offline multi-seed results.

M1.justification: The softmax encoder, linear decoder, Gram reconstruction objective, convex bases, and offline addition, online addition, and negation procedures remain unchanged. The WEMoE compatibility explanation and QLoRA experiment apply the existing framework; the unconstrained encoder is an ablation.

E1.justification: The same vision, language, six-target OOD, generative, continual-learning, and negation coverage is retained. The new precision, QLoRA, and encoder experiments reuse the existing eight vision tasks without introducing new task requirements or populations.

E2.justification: v5 Table 5 adds Gradient Ascent to the existing negation comparison. Table 20 adds an unconstrained linear-encoder comparator. The other evaluated comparator sets are retained; WEMoE is described as compatible but is not newly benchmarked.

E3.justification: New configurations test FP32, FP16, BF16, and 4-bit QLoRA with rank 16 and alpha 32 on ViT-B/16, eight tasks, and four bases. Profiling adds phase timings and memory measurements. Existing subsampling, few-shot budgets, coefficient searches, and merging hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v5 substantially broadens supplementary validation: the encoder ablation isolates the softmax constraint, precision and QLoRA experiments test compression compatibility, detailed profiling examines construction overhead, and offline multi-seed comparisons assess stability. The earlier temperature, subsampling, weighting, basis-count, and checkpoint-mixing analyses remain.

E5.justification: v4 already reports three-run average timings and five-task-order-run continual results with standard deviations. v5 retains these and adds offline L&S versus L&S-AE means and standard errors over three seeds across architectures and task counts in Table 15.

E6.justification: A substantial set of additional results is reported, while matched older scores remain unchanged. Examples include softmax versus linear normalized accuracy of 71.7% versus 54.6% (Table 20), QLoRA AE versus TA accuracy of 0.565 versus 0.566 (Table 19), and Gradient Ascent target/control accuracy of 0.027/0.003 on ViT-B/32 (Table 5). Precision, memory, timing, and multi-seed results are also added.

T1.justification: The main theorem bounds and Appendix B proofs are largely retained. However, v5 introduces epsilon as the maximum absolute task-vector inner product divided by C squared in Section 3.2.3, differing from the appendix's cosine-bound assumption. Appendix C also adds an equivalence argument for computing statistics on mixed basis data.

C1.justification: Compression, arithmetic compatibility, reconstruction-dependent guarantees, and advantages over heuristic bases remain the central claims. The introduction's new 'in some settings' qualifier repeats a qualification already present in v4's abstract; the revised unlearning wording continues to describe the same error bounds.

C2.justification: Rewritten Remark 3.8 explains that the pretrained model already has a comparable loss bound and relates useful guarantees to modest fine-tuning gains. v5 also interprets Gradient Ascent's control-performance collapse, discusses precision and QLoRA tradeoffs, and explicitly notes that orthogonality alone cannot guarantee successful merging.

D1.justification: v5 adds phase-level timing, CPU/GPU memory, and artifact-size information in Table 11, plus precision and QLoRA configuration details. Appendix C expands implementation explanations. The default AE hyperparameters, A6000 hardware disclosure, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 5.3 positions the framework relative to LoRA, QLoRA, QA-LoRA, EoRA, and CLoQ; additional citations cover safety-related negation applications. Sections 5.2 and 5.4 largely relocate the existing low-rank/subspace and matrix-factorization discussions from v4 Appendices A.3 and A.4.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative remain intact. Changes include targeted theoretical explanations, reorganized related work, assumptions summarized in the main text, a broader-impact paragraph, terminology corrections, and updated author and publication information.

P2.justification: The TMLR template changes typography, text width, headers, author layout, and page flow throughout. v4 Table 5 moves into the main text as v5 Table 1 with a WEMoE row. New profiling, precision, multi-seed, QLoRA, and ablation tables expand the displays, and the negation table gains a row. Figures 1–12 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The encoder ablation, offline uncertainty estimates, and practical compression measurements provide stronger support for the existing design and efficiency claims than v4 supplied. These are useful, focused improvements alongside clearer discussion of the theoretical bounds. Their benefit outweighs the localized new inconsistency between the main-text similarity definition and Appendix B, but does not amount to a substantial overall transformation.
